description: Phase-ONB — LLM-driven self-onboarding. New operator clones Aura, runs setup wizard (Telegram token + LLM creds), opens Telegram and /start — Aura herself interviews them in their language and writes SOUL/AGENT/USER overlays via workspace_write. Single conversation, ~5-7 turns, self-demonstrating (operator sees Aura's real tools in action). Replaces the current 'find empty runtime-workspace, write 3 markdown files by hand' onboarding gap. Research docs: docs/onboarding-research/{local-patterns,state-of-art}-2026-05-20.md (openhuman welcome agent pattern + Pi/Claude/Andoria production patterns + arxiv refs). KEY DESIGN: prompt-overlay swap in agentloop (NOT separate agent class), soft state machine in the prompt (NOT in Go), passive language detection, finalize_onboarding tool with server-side validation (single-worst-failure-mode = exit without calling it per openhuman issue #1123). 2 stories — A01 substrate (prompt+migration+tool+swap), A02 hardening (probe+golden+localized fallback templates). NO Phase-U plugin loader in this phase (overlays still raw markdown files); plugin shape comes later. STRICT one-story-exit per scripts/ralph/CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: Welcome system-prompt overlay + finalize_onboarding tool + migration v27 + agentloop trigger
userStories.description: Ship the complete onboarding substrate in one atomic commit. Five components: (a) MIGRATION v27 — new SQLite column `chat_onboarding_completed BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE` on the existing settings table (NOT a new table — reuse settings key-value pattern with key='chat_onboarding_completed'). Backward compat: rows without the key read as false. (b) WELCOME PROMPT — new file internal/onboarding/welcome.md (~150-180 lines markdown, //go:embed'd into Go via `//go:embed welcome.md`). Adapted from D:/tmp/openhuman/src/openhuman/agent/agents/welcome/prompt.md with these CHANGES: Italian-default voice with passive language detection from first user turn; goal swapped from 'connect 1+ app' to 'compile SOUL.md + AGENT.md + USER.md via workspace_write'; tool set narrowed to {workspace_write, finalize_onboarding} only; budget targets baked in (SOUL ~400w first-person, AGENT ~300w runtime contract, USER ~200w preferences); explicit 5-question target with 10-question ceiling; escape hatch ('skippa', 'just defaults', 'lasciamo perdere'); single-question-per-turn rule; ≤3-sentence reply rule; no markdown formatting in chat replies (Telegram-friendly plain prose); explicit 'You can't do real work yet' guard (the welcome agent must refuse search/web/exec until onboarding completes); proactive opening trigger string 'Operatore al primo contatto. Lingua sconosciuta. Avvia onboarding.' that the welcome prompt recognizes and responds to with a warm Italian opener. (c) AGENTLOOP TRIGGER — in internal/chat/agentloop.go (or wherever the system prompt is built — grep for the prompt builder entry point), add a top check: `if !settings.ChatOnboardingCompleted && allOverlaysEmptyOrMissing(SOUL, AGENT, USER) { systemPrompt = welcome.Prompt(); toolWhitelist = []string{"workspace_write", "finalize_onboarding"} } else { normal prompt builder }`. The whitelist gate is critical — during onboarding, search_memory/web/exec must be UNAVAILABLE so the welcome agent can't drift into 'real work' (openhuman hard rule lines 109-111). (d) FINALIZE_ONBOARDING TOOL — new file internal/agent/tools/registry/finalize_onboarding.go (~120 LOC). Tool name 'finalize_onboarding', params: `{action: 'compile' | 'skip'}`. On action='compile': (i) read SOUL.md, AGENT.md, USER.md from PROMPT_OVERLAY_PATH; (ii) validate — each file ≥50 bytes AND USER.md contains a non-placeholder Name + Language line (regex check: `(?i)^(name|nome)\s*:\s*\S+` and `(?i)^(language|lingua)\s*:\s*\S+`); (iii) if validation fails, return ToolResult.Error('Cannot finalize: USER.md missing name or language — ask the user') so the agent can re-ask; (iv) if pass, settings_update chat_onboarding_completed=true; (v) emit a structured success message that the agent can use as final farewell + pin to Telegram. On action='skip': workspace_write × 3 minimal placeholder files (//go:embed default-templates auto-localized to detected language using a tiny it/en switch — defer other languages to A02), then settings_update. ALWAYS run on the next user message: the normal main-agent path resumes seamlessly. (e) TESTS — internal/onboarding/welcome_test.go covers: prompt-embed loads; the trigger condition produces the welcome prompt vs normal prompt across the 4 truth-table cases (completed=true overlays-empty, completed=true overlays-present, completed=false overlays-empty, completed=false overlays-present); finalize_onboarding compile validation rejects missing-name USER.md + accepts valid USER.md; skip path writes 3 non-empty files. NO probe_chat case yet — that's US-ONB-A02. NO real Telegram E2E — A02. NO localized templates beyond IT/EN — A02.

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read docs/onboarding-research/local-patterns-2026-05-20.md IN FULL — the Aura sketch sections (a)(b)(c)(d) are the implementation guide. (2) Read docs/onboarding-research/state-of-art-2026-05-20.md sections 'Concrete recommendation for Aura' onwards. (3) Read D:/tmp/openhuman/src/openhuman/agent/agents/welcome/prompt.md IN FULL — adapt it line-by-line for Aura (Italian voice, workspace_write goal, narrower tool set). (4) Read internal/chat/agentloop.go to find the prompt-builder entry point. (5) Read internal/agent/tools/registry/ for the tool registration pattern (e.g. search_memory.go as template). (6) Read internal/db/migrations/migrations.go for the migration shape (v23 add_chat_settings_voice_mode is precedent). PROMPT WRITING DISCIPLINE: don't translate openhuman's prompt mechanically — adapt the voice + the goal. Italian first-person warmth: 'Ciao! Sono Aura. È il nostro primo contatto e vorrei conoscerti un po' prima di metterci al lavoro insieme. Come ti chiami e cosa vorresti farmi diventare per te?' as opener template. Then: ONE question per turn. Stop conditions: ≥5 questions answered AND name+language confirmed in conversation history. WHITELIST IMPLEMENTATION: the cleanest mechanism for Aura today is probably to wrap the existing tool registry with a filter when in onboarding mode — `registry.SubsetForOnboarding()` returning only the 2 allowed tools. Don't reach for capability gates ([[project_target_architecture_diagram_2026-05-15]] mentions internal/identity capabilities — that's heavier than needed here). FINALIZE_ONBOARDING SHAPE: this tool should be in the registry but ONLY surfaced when in onboarding mode. After onboarding completes, it can stay registered but never invoked (the trigger condition prevents the agent from being in a state where it would call it). Tests should cover the 'tool called after onboarding already completed' edge case — return ToolResult.Error('already completed'). SCOPE DISCIPLINE: NO probe_chat case in this story — that's A02. NO Phase-U plugin loader — overlays stay raw markdown files. NO multi-locale defaults beyond IT/EN — A02 extends. NO welcome wiki page seeding (the 'here's what Aura can do' page) — defer to A02 too. INVARIANT: an EXISTING deployment with chat_onboarding_completed=true (or NULL → reads as false BUT overlays present) MUST not trigger onboarding mode. The trigger requires both flag=false AND overlays empty. Davide's current dev setup has overlays present → won't trip. Verify with TestWelcomeTriggerConditionTable case 4.

userStories.title: Welcome flow probe + golden conversation fixture + localized fallback templates
userStories.description: Harden Phase-ONB with regression coverage + multi-language defaults. (a) PROBE CASE — new cmd/probe_chat/cases.go entry 'onboarding_welcome_full_flow'. Setup: spin up a fresh Aura instance with chat_onboarding_completed=false + empty runtime-workspace; run a scripted 6-turn conversation that answers a synthetic operator's persona (name='TestOp', language='it', role='developer', communication='casual', preferred_gender_for_aura='femminile'); assert each turn's reply respects the welcome rules (single question, ≤3 sentences, no markdown, Italian voice); after turn 6 the operator says 'ok va bene così', expect the agent to call finalize_onboarding(action='compile'); verify SOUL.md + AGENT.md + USER.md are written with non-empty content matching the budget targets (SOUL 300-500 words, AGENT 200-400 words, USER 100-300 words); USER.md contains 'TestOp' + 'italiano'; settings chat_onboarding_completed flipped to true; next agent invocation uses the normal prompt path (verify by checking the system prompt rendered for a follow-up turn doesn't contain the welcome prompt header). (b) GOLDEN FIXTURE — cmd/probe_chat/fixtures/onboarding_golden_conversation_it.json captures the expected request/response shape across all 6 turns (paraphrase-tolerant via fuzzy assertions on key phrases: opener mentions 'Aura' + asks name; turn 2 mentions language; turn 3 mentions role; etc.). Operator-only flag -update-golden regenerates against current LLM behavior. (c) LOCALIZED FALLBACK TEMPLATES — extend internal/onboarding/defaults/ with embedded markdown files: defaults/it/SOUL.md, defaults/it/AGENT.md, defaults/it/USER.md, defaults/en/SOUL.md, defaults/en/AGENT.md, defaults/en/USER.md. Used by finalize_onboarding(action='skip') when the operator bails. Each template is the MINIMUM viable overlay (~50 lines markdown with friendly placeholder content explaining 'fill me in' in the operator's detected language). (d) WELCOME WIKI SEED — on successful compile, finalize_onboarding additionally creates a single wiki page wiki/benvenuto-su-aura.md (or 'welcome-to-aura.md' if EN) with a 200-300 word intro to Aura's capabilities (memory, tools, scheduler, sources, web search) — gives the new operator something to read first. (e) PROBE SKIP GATE — the case SKIPS (not fails) when no LLM provider is reachable from the probe context, matching the existing probe_chat pattern. (f) DOC — extend docs/onboarding-research/ or create docs/onboarding-runbook.md with: how to manually reset onboarding for testing (DELETE FROM settings WHERE key='chat_onboarding_completed' + rm runtime-workspace/*.md), how to interpret probe results, how to update fallback templates.

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read US-ONB-A01's committed code — this story extends, not replaces. (2) Read cmd/probe_chat/main.go + cmd/probe_chat/cases.go for the case-shape template. (3) Read cmd/probe_chat/fixtures/*.json for the fixture-shape template (probably none today for multi-turn; this story may need to invent the 6-turn fixture shape — keep it simple: array of {turn_index, user_say, expected_reply_contains_any_of, expected_tool_calls}). FUZZY ASSERTION DISCIPLINE: paraphrase-tolerant means the test asserts 'reply contains ANY of [\"come ti chiami\", \"qual è il tuo nome\", \"posso sapere il tuo nome\"]' for the name question, not exact string. Document the rationale in the fixture file header comment. LOCALIZED DEFAULTS WRITING DISCIPLINE: these templates are the MINIMUM viable overlay — friendly + placeholder-clear. Italian default SOUL: 'Sono Aura. (Aggiungi qui chi sono e come parlo — questo file definisce la mia voce.)'. Don't make them long. Don't try to be clever. The whole point of the skip path is 'I just want defaults to start, I'll customize later'. WIKI SEED CONTENT: keep it short, factual, Aura-voice. Sections: 'Cosa posso fare' (memory + tools + scheduler), 'Come parlare con me' (Telegram + dashboard), 'Cosa NON posso fare oggi' (set expectations honestly — be explicit about Phase-MM Wave 3 audio not yet shipped, etc.). PROBE FRAGILITY: LLM-driven probes are inherently flaky on prose. The fuzzy assertions are designed to tolerate it. If a turn's reply matches NONE of the acceptable variants, fail with the actual reply printed for the operator to either fix the prompt OR add a new acceptable variant to the fixture. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: NO additional languages beyond IT/EN in this story (future PRs can add ES/FR/DE/PT — pattern is established). NO dashboard panel showing onboarding state — operator only sees it during the chat. NO retry-on-validation-failure UI — the welcome agent already handles re-asking via the validation error message. NO E2E real-Telegram test — too flaky, skip until a deterministic harness exists. INVARIANT: this story's probe must work against the same docker compose stack the rest of probe_chat uses. No new sidecar dependencies. No new env vars beyond what A01 already added.
